content: 1. Fosphenytoin and Norethindrone Acetate: Fosphenytoin reduces the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. Hormonal contraceptives may become unreliable for effective birth control when co-administered. Additionally, this combination may increase the risk of menstrual-related adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. Avoid co-administration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. If used together, monitor closely. 2. Fostemsavir and Elagolix: Fostemsavir increases the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters. Avoid co-administration if possible, or adjust the dose of OATP1B1/3 substrates when used with fostemsavir. Monitor therapy closely. 3. Elagolix and Fruquintinib: Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of fruquintinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers is unavoidable, continue fruquintinib at the recommended dosage. 4. Elagolix and Ganaxolone: Elagolix reduces the levels or effects of ganaxolone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers. If unavoidable, consider increasing the ganaxolone dose but do not exceed the maximum daily dose based on weight. Monitor closely. 5. Elagolix and Gefitinib: Elagolix decreases gefitinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if necessary. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 6. Gemfibrozil and Elagolix: Gemfibrozil increases elagolix levels by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters. Co-administration of elagolix with strong OATP1B1 inhibitors is contraindicated. 7. Elagolix and Glasdegib: Elagolix reduces glasdegib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 8. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir and Elagolix: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases elagolix levels by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters. Co-administration is contraindicated. Elagolix also decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 9. Grapefruit and Elagolix: Grapefruit increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely. 10. Elagolix and Guanfacine: Elagolix decreases guanfacine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if necessary. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 11. Elagolix and Haloperidol: Elagolix reduces haloperidol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 12. Elagolix and Hydrocodone: Elagolix decreases hydrocodone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if necessary. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 13. Elagolix and Hydrocortisone: Elagolix increases hydrocortisone levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Elagolix and Hydroxyprogesterone Caproate: Elagolix reduces hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 15. Elagolix and Ibrutinib: Elagolix decreases ibrutinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if necessary. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 16. Elagolix and Idarubicin: Elagolix increases idarubicin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Idelalisib and Elagolix: Idelalisib increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Limit elagolix dose to 150 mg daily and restrict CYP3A inhibitor use to six months if co-administered. Monitor closely. 18. Elagolix and Iloperidone: Iloperidone increases norethindrone acetate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may elevate plasma levels of drugs primarily metabolized by CYP3A4. Monitor closely. 19. Elagolix and Imatinib: Elagolix decreases imatinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if necessary. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 20. Elagolix and Imipramine: Elagolix increases imipramine levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution with sensitive CYP2C19 substrates. Monitor closely. 21. Elagolix and Indinavir: Elagolix decreases indinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Monitor closely. 22. Elagolix and Infigratinib: Elagolix decreases infigratinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely. 23. Norethindrone Acetate and Insulin: Norethindrone acetate reduces the effects of insulin (including insulin degludec, insulin aspart, and inhaled insulin) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Elagolix and Irinotecan: Elagolix decreases irinotecan levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if necessary. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 25. Elagolix and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Monitor closely. 26. Elagolix and Ivabradine: Elagolix decreases ivabradine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if necessary. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 27. Elagolix and Ivosidenib: Ivosidenib decreases elagolix levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates or replace with alternative therapies. Monitor closely. 28. Elagolix and Ketamine: Elagolix decreases ketamine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if necessary. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 29. Ketoconazole and Elagolix: Ketoconazole increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Limit elagolix dose to 150 mg daily and restrict CYP3A inhibitor use to six months if co-administered. Monitor closely. 30. Elagolix and Lacosamide: Elagolix decreases lacosamide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if necessary. Adjust therapy and monitor closely.
